output.narrative_summary: This result rests on the link from Delivery Throughput to Operating Margin. If throughput shifts, more runs could support a different option. In this model, 53% of runs supported Move to Four Day Week, and the options are close.

story_headlines.opt_four_day: Move to Four Day Week gains when delivery throughput and staff retention both hold up well.
story_headlines.opt_status_quo: Keep Current Schedule would draw more support if delivery throughput proves weaker than modelled.

robustness_explanation.summary: The ordering holds in about 56% of variations, so this sits on the fragile side based on current estimates.
robustness_explanation.primary_risk: The link from Delivery Throughput to Operating Margin is the main source of fragility here.
stability_factors: Staff Retention shows a reasonably well evidenced connection to Operating Margin.
fragility_factors: The link from Delivery Throughput to Operating Margin could shift which option more runs support.

output.readiness_rationale: Two things still hold this back: the close split between the options and the unsettled link from Delivery Throughput to Operating Margin, which together leave the comparison open to change.

fac_throughput.specific_action: Pull recent delivery throughput records and compare actual completion rates against the modelled estimate.
fac_throughput.rationale: Throughput is the main swing factor behind this comparison, so firming it up directly sharpens the result.
fac_throughput.decision_hygiene: Estimate the current throughput rate yourself before checking the records.

edge_throughput_margin.trigger_description: If Delivery Throughput weakens relative to the connection assumed with Operating Margin...
edge_throughput_margin.consequence: ...then the most runs would support Keep Current Schedule rather than Move to Four Day Week.

flip_thresholds.narrative: If Delivery Throughput moves from 44% to 49%, more runs would support a different option.

key_assumptions: The link from Delivery Throughput to Operating Margin assumes current working patterns continue unchanged.
The link from Staff Retention to Operating Margin assumes retention effects show up within the modelled period.

decision_quality_prompts.question: This failed because delivery throughput dropped after the change, what early signs would have warned you?
decision_quality_prompts.applies_because: The comparison is close and still open, so imagining failure now surfaces what to watch before acting.

decision_quality_prompts.question: How would choosing Move to Four Day Week feel in 10 minutes, 10 months, and 10 years?
decision_quality_prompts.applies_because: The two options sit close together on this model, so weighing the choice across different time horizons helps separate short term reaction from lasting effect.

pre_mortem.failure_scenario: This failed because Delivery Throughput weakened after the move, pulling Operating Margin down further than the model assumed.
warning_signs: Delivery throughput tracking below the modelled rate in the weeks after the change.
Operating margin slipping against plan without a clear retention offset.
pre_mortem.mitigation: Monitor delivery throughput closely in the first weeks after any change and compare it against the modelled rate.
pre_mortem.review_trigger: Reconvene if delivery throughput falls short of the modelled rate before the next planning cycle.
